alignments.note: Rule 22: the substantival article corresponds to the English pronoun.
The ASV writes no word for γάρ here.

Rule 39's test: the single English can spells both the modal particle and δύναμαι, so the pair is one aligned unit. Splitting can onto ἄν and leaving δυναίμην only the subject pronoun is the competing reading; rule 50 forbids leaving ἄν unrepresented either way.
Rule 39: ἐὰν μή rendered by the single conjunction except.
Rule 17: one is the generic completion of the indefinite, which keeps the head.
Rule 61: no preposition governs the infinitive, so to is its helper; up realizes the preverb ἀνα- under rule 106.

Rule 88: the ASV converts the subordinate participle ἀναβάντα into a coordinate member, so the supplied juncture and is a rule 7 helper on the verb it introduces and is not added; head on sit. Rule 98 is the competing reading and would make and added, but it is scoped to an asyndetic seam between two like constituents both rendered alike, and here the members are a participle and an infinitive with the participle carrying the subordination rule 88 says licenses the juncture. Rule 29 does not apply, rule 98 having confined it to a compound numeral.

review_notes: ἄν and δυναίμην joined because the ASV wrote only can for both; the unit's note names the competing split.

The juncture and before sit is read under rule 88 rather than rule 29, which rule 98 forbids as a general licence: ἀναβάντα is a subordinate participle the ASV rewrote as a coordinate member, and that participle is the licensing token. Rule 98's added reading is named in the unit's note as the competitor, its own scope being two like constituents both rendered alike.
